teaching_point: Day 1 case: KE — superficial air-filled blisters burst to leave expanding collarettes of scale on palm/fingers; no erythema, no itch.

teaching_point: KE — dry lamellar peeling across volar fingers; non-inflamed; recurs every few weeks, often worse in summer/with sweaty palms.

teaching_point: KE — fingertip peeling/shallow cracks; deeper split at fingertips can feel hard and numb (matches Day 1 numbness).

teaching_point: Chronic palmar hand eczema — scale, fissuring and erythema on both palms; contrast with non-inflamed KE.

teaching_point: Irritant contact dermatitis from wet work — dry, glazed, fissured palmar fingers; commonest cause of occupational hand eczema.

teaching_point: Chronic hand eczema on dorsal fingers — thickening, dryness, scale (lichenification) in skin of colour.

teaching_point: Patch-test reading with several positives — needed in persistent hand eczema to separate ACD (e.g. chromate in cement, rubber accelerators) from ICD.

teaching_point: Positive patch test to a piece of rubber glove at 48 h — glove (thiuram/carbamate) allergy in workers who wear protective gloves.

teaching_point: Secondarily infected hand dermatitis — crusting/weeping; swab and treat infection; complication of fissured chronic eczema.

teaching_point: Palmar hyperlinearity — exaggerated palm creases (atopic marker / chronic rubbing); the Day 2 stem uses this term for lichenified palms.

teaching_point: Pompholyx — deep-seated 1–2 mm "tapioca" vesicles on palm; intensely itchy; resolves with peeling over 2–3 weeks.
dermnet_caption: Discrete vesicles and blisters on the palmar skin
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Discrete vesicles and blisters on the palmar skin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dyshidrotic-eczema

teaching_point: Pompholyx — vesicles and blisters along sides of fingers; symmetrical; DDx tinea (unilateral → take scrapings).
dermnet_caption: Vesicles and blisters on the fingers in vesicular eczema
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Vesicles and blisters on the fingers in vesicular eczema (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dyshidrotic-eczema

teaching_point: Podopompholyx — extensive vesiculation/blistering on soles; check toe webs for tinea pedis (dermatophytide).
dermnet_caption: Extensive vesiculation and blistering on the soles - vesicular eczema is usually symmetrical
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Extensive vesiculation and blistering on the soles - vesicular eczema is usually symmetrical (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dyshidrotic-eczema

teaching_point: PPP — sterile yellow pustules evolving to rusty-brown macules in a scaly plaque; strongly linked with smoking.
dermnet_caption: Pustules and rusty dots in a scaly plaque typical of PPP
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pustules and rusty dots in a scaly plaque typical of PPP (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/palmoplantar-pustulosis

teaching_point: PPP on the palm — pustules on thenar/central palm; sterile (culture negative).
dermnet_caption: Pustules on the palm due to PPP
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pustules on the palm due to PPP (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/palmoplantar-pustulosis

teaching_point: PPP on soles — redness, scale, pustules and brown dots on instep/heel; often bilateral.
dermnet_caption: Typical lesions of PPP on the soles - redness, scale, pustules, and rusty red dots
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Typical lesions of PPP on the soles - redness, scale, pustules, and rusty red dots (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/palmoplantar-pustulosis

teaching_point: Palmar psoriasis — well-demarcated red scaly plaques with sharp border; check nails, scalp, elbows; may be hard to tell from hyperkeratotic eczema.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Palmar psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/psoriasis-of-the-palms-and-soles

teaching_point: Plantar psoriasis — thick scale with fissuring on weight-bearing soles; DDx moccasin tinea pedis (send scrapings).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Plantar psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/psoriasis-of-the-palms-and-soles

teaching_point: Palmoplantar psoriasis — symmetrical hyperkeratosis with fissures; associated with nail dystrophy and psoriatic arthritis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Palmoplantar psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/psoriasis-of-the-palms-and-soles

teaching_point: Hyperkeratotic tinea manuum — usually one palm; white scale in creases; "two feet–one hand" — look at feet.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tinea manuum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-manuum

teaching_point: Inflammatory (zoophilic) tinea on finger/hand — raised active edge; ask about animal contact.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tinea manuum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-manuum

teaching_point: Tinea on dorsal hand — annular plaques with active edge; contiguous palm/dorsum involvement suggests fungus not eczema.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tinea manuum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-manuum

teaching_point: Moccasin tinea pedis — diffuse fine white scale over soles/sides; reservoir for tinea manuum; key DDx of plantar psoriasis/KE.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Moccasin tinea pedis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-pedis

teaching_point: Interdigital tinea pedis with onychomycosis — check toe webs and nails in any palmoplantar rash.

attribution: Image: DermNet — Tinea pedis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-pedis

teaching_point: Day 4 case: EM — round, well-demarcated papules/early targets on limb (acral-first then spreads centripetally).
